checks.name: a5-starvation-bound-and-negative-control
checks.summary: This is the M7 condition TestDecidePreventsDoubleOwnerAndIsolatesFailureStorm does not prove (that test proves failure-storm ISOLATION of an unhealthy repository; this proves STARVATION prevention between two equally HEALTHY repositories under pure capacity contention). Scenario: 20 same-priority flood Requirements in repo-flood permanently retried (reset to Ready each tick) against one high-value Requirement ('important', ValueScore=50/UrgencyScore=10, static score 23500) in repo-important, one Runner (capacity 1) shared, one Repository each healthy (no isolation involved). Positive: 'important's StarvationRisk is raised +5/tick; measured result: assigned on tick 4 of the StarvationBoundTicks=5 bound (log: "'important' was assigned on tick 4 (bound=5)") -- PASS. StarvationBoundTicks=5 was derived, before this measurement, from weightStarvationRisk=500 being the largest single weight (documented in scheduler.go/priority.go) needing to close a fixed 6500-point deficit in <=3 increments of 2500 each, i.e. within a small bound, with a 1-tick margin. Negative control: with scoreFn swapped (via a save/restore of the package-level scoreFn variable) to an otherwise-identical scorer that omits only the StarvationRisk term, the IDENTICAL scenario including the identical per-tick StarvationRisk increments never converges within the same 5-tick bound, nor within 20x that bound (100 ticks) -- PASS, proving the positive result is caused by the StarvationRisk term (age is a no-op here since every candidate shares one CreatedAt, so it cancels out of the comparison).

checks.name: a6-cross-repository-rollback-convergence

(c) A third Decide/Apply cycle from the now-Assigned snapshot produces an empty Plan and Apply of it is reflect.DeepEqual to its input, proving convergence rather than oscillation -- PASS.

no duplicate owner for the same Increment | TestDecidePreventsDoubleOwnerAndIsolatesFailureStorm and the owned()/already-owned Reason path prove Decide never assigns a second Claim to an Increment/Requirement that already owns one, within one Decide call and one Apply | that two independent Runner execution entities cannot BOTH believe they own the same Increment when they cannot see each other's in-flight state (a real race, not a sequential in-memory check) -- requires the two-entity substrate V2-031 owns
no starvation of other important Requirements under one Repository's failure storm | TestStarvationBoundAssignsWaitingHighValueRequirementWithinBoundTicks and its negative control (TestStarvationNegativeControlFailsToConvergeWithoutStarvationRiskTerm) prove, under an injected clock with a bounded tick loop, that a healthy second Repository's high-value Requirement is assigned within StarvationBoundTicks=5 ticks despite a same-tick-capacity flood from a first Repository, and that the identical scenario never converges once the StarvationRisk term is neutralised | that this bound holds when the flood and the waiter are driven by two independent Runner execution entities with real wall-clock timing and independent failure/retry timing, not a single sequential loop
